rec.name: Purchase Affirmation CTA ("Good choice!")
rec.status: Reference only (benchmark from Snocks shop; no spec or build documented)

what.text: A CTA button that praises the shopper's decision with a short affirmation, "Gute Wahl! 👍" ("Good choice!" with a thumbs-up emoji), instead of a purely functional label. In the Snocks reference it is a large, full-width, outlined button with centered dark text. It sits directly below a green stock line ("Auf Lager - in 1-3 Werktagen bei dir", i.e. "In stock - with you in 1-3 working days") and a light grey newsletter strip ("Jetzt Newsletter abonnieren und bis zu 30% sichern", i.e. "Subscribe to our newsletter now and save up to 30%"). The ticket does not say whether the affirmation is the button's default label or a state shown after the shopper selects a variant or adds to cart.

why.text: Positive reinforcement of the decision reduces post-decision doubt and adds a friendly, brand-personality moment at the point of commitment. Affirming the choice makes the shopper feel validated and more likely to continue. The delivery-time line above the button adds reassurance. The effect is likely small and mainly emotional, and it is unproven in this ticket.

how.text: Likely implementation (inferred): use a button label or state that swaps to the affirmation text (plus emoji) once the shopper makes a selection or clicks add-to-cart. Style it as an outlined, full-width button with a dark 2px border and rounded corners. Place it below the stock/delivery line and the optional promo strip. The ticket gives no acceptance criteria; the only instruction is "see Snocks shop". The trigger, the exact behaviour (does the button still add to cart?) and the copy variants must be defined before building.

items: Trigger: default label vs. after variant selection vs. after add-to-cart
Button style: outlined vs. filled, border colour, radius
Show or hide the newsletter promo strip above the button

dependencies.text: No metafields or apps are documented. The stock line implies inventory-based messaging. The newsletter strip ("up to 30%") implies an existing newsletter incentive or popup/Klaviyo-type setup. Theme must allow custom button label states (JS).

items: Newsletter signup rate (if the promo strip is shown)

images.caption: Snocks reference: green stock/delivery line, grey newsletter promo strip, and outlined "Gute Wahl! 👍" CTA button
